newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed ahead of report.

text.p: CME live cattle futures held mixed price levels into the close ahead of the Cattle-on-Feed report with back months down. Feeders followed the action in deferred live cattle on report expectations, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.325 cent higher to 0.225 lower with February up most and April up 0.100 at 66.450 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.275 to 0.050 lower with March off 0.225 at 67.950 cents.

February live cattle held firm following the strong tone to cash cattle the past week and this supported nearbys. However, deferreds ranged lower on evening up trade ahead of the report, traders said.
The report could show heavy placements during January and larger than year ago on-feed cattle supplies, they said.

The average analyst estimate on the report for cattle on feed at major 7-state feedlots of 1,000 head or more for February 1 was 103.9 percent in a range of 101.5 to 105.4 percent. The estimate for January placements averaged 107.5 percent and ranged from 99 to 114.6 percent and January marketings averaged 101.3 percent and ranged from 99 to 104 percent of last year.

Feeder cattle futures continued to follow the lead of live cattle in thin dealings. If placements were large in January and on-feed numbers increased, demand for feeders will likely be reduced going into the spring.
A lower CME feeder cattle index also weighed on the market, they said. The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.19 at $69.00 per cwt.

Spreading accounted for part of the early volume before trading turned very light. R.J. O'Brien sold April while Cargill Investor Services and RBH bought April feeders and sold October live cattle, pit sources said.
Futures will be closed Monday in observance of Presidents' Day and resume trade on Tuesday.
